sections.content: How many people are "industrial cleaning process occupations"?

20,195 people

were counted on the census as "industrial cleaning process occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Industrial cleaning process occupations clean manufactured goods, plant and machinery, and industrial, commercial and other premises.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "industrial cleaning process occupations" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "industrial cleaning process occupations", 12.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "industrial cleaning process occupations" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "industrial cleaning process occupations" included:

  • butchers
  • pre-press technicians
  • welding trades

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "industrial cleaning process occupations" there were more men than women (75.4% compared with 24.6%).

This means "industrial cleaning process occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 75.4% and women made up 24.6% of "industrial cleaning process occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "industrial cleaning process occupations" included:

  • IT managers
  • production, factory and assembly supervisors
  • postal workers, mail sorters and messengers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "industrial cleaning process occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "industrial cleaning process occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "industrial cleaning process occupations", 10.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75% compared with 25%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.9%) than self-employed (7.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leicester, this is in the same region of the East Midlands.
